claims.statement: The auth API surface lives under app/api/auth/ as Next.js App Router handlers and consists of exactly ten routes: signin/vercel (POST), signin/github (GET, unified), github/signin (GET and POST, legacy), callback/vercel (GET), github/callback (GET), info (GET), rate-limit (GET), github/status (GET), github/disconnect (POST), and signout (GET). Each route exports only the HTTP methods listed.

The Vercel sign-in route uses the arctic library's OAuth2Client with createAuthorizationURLWithPKCE (CodeChallengeMethod.S256), generateState, and generateCodeVerifier; the callback exchanges the code by calling validateAuthorizationCode against Vercel's bespoke token endpoint at https://vercel.com/api/login/oauth/token because arctic ships no Vercel adapter, and it writes the short-lived vercel_oauth_state, vercel_oauth_code_verifier, and vercel_oauth_redirect_to cookies (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production, 10-minute maxAge) before returning JSON { url }.

The GitHub flow uses three coexisting cookie sets that the callback disambiguates by the presence of github_auth_mode: the unified signin/connect set (github_auth_state, github_auth_redirect_to, github_auth_mode) optionally with github_oauth_user_id for connect, the legacy connect-only set (github_oauth_state, github_oauth_redirect_to, github_oauth_user_id) written by /api/auth/github/signin, and the connecting-user-id cookie github_oauth_user_id that both flows share; all are HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production, with a 10-minute TTL, and the legacy branch exists only so a deploy does not break browsers mid-OAuth.

The GitHub callback dispatches on github_auth_mode: in signin mode it calls createGitHubSession (which upserts a users row with encrypted accessToken and writes the JWE session cookie), and in connect mode it encrypts the new token and branches on three sub-cases against the accounts table — same-user update, conflict where the GitHub identity belongs to another internal user (reparent tasks/connectors/accounts/keys and delete the old users row), or fresh INSERT — with the legacy no-auth-mode path treated as implicit connect.

The legacy /api/auth/github/signin route exposes both GET and POST for browser versus fetch callers: GET redirects directly to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with the github_oauth_* cookies set, while POST returns { url } as JSON for programmatic callers like redirectToSignIn-style helpers, and both require an existing session (GET redirects to / for unauthenticated users; POST returns 401 JSON).

/api/auth/info is provider-aware: for a GitHub-primary session it returns the existing session verbatim, for a Vercel-primary session it rehydrates by reading the encrypted token through getOAuthToken(userId, 'vercel') and re-running createSession (refreshing profile data on every page load), and for no session it returns { user: undefined } while emitting the immediate-expiry Set-Cookie via saveSession(response, undefined); the route picks saveSession vs. saveGitHubSession based on session.authProvider.

/api/auth/signout walks four steps: read the session via getSessionFromReq, fetch the upstream token via getOAuthToken keyed by session.authProvider, revoke the token at the provider (DELETE https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/token with HTTP Basic auth for GitHub, or POST https://vercel.com/api/login/oauth/token/revoke with form-urlencoded body for Vercel, both using client credentials as Basic auth), then return { url } and call saveSession(response, undefined) to emit the immediate-expiry cookie — revoke failures are logged but the local cookie is always cleared.

POST /api/auth/github/disconnect refuses with 400 'Cannot disconnect primary authentication method' when session.authProvider === 'github', because deleting the only account row would leave a session whose underlying users.accessToken is gone; the component layer in components/auth/sign-out.tsx only renders the Disconnect menu item for Vercel users, so the route handler's guard is a second line of defense rather than the user-facing rule.

/api/auth/rate-limit delegates to checkRateLimit in lib/utils/rate-limit.ts, which sums today's non-soft-deleted tasks and taskMessages.role = 'user' rows and returns { allowed, remaining, total, resetAt } where resetAt is the next UTC midnight; the dropdown in components/auth/sign-out.tsx renders this as '{remaining}/{total} messages remaining today' on every open.

GET /api/auth/github/status returns one of three shapes by checking both storage buckets for the current session: { connected: false } when no session or no GitHub identity, { connected: true, username, connectedAt } when an accounts row exists with provider='github' (linked), or the same shape when the user's users row has provider='github' (primary), so the UI can render a single Connected badge for either bucket.

components/auth/session-provider.tsx is the polling loop that keeps the Jotai sessionAtom and githubConnectionAtom warm: on mount it fetches /api/auth/info and /api/auth/github/status in parallel, then re-fetches both every 60 seconds and on every window.focus event; the auth UI split between SignIn and SignOut is decided by the session atom with a SSR-friendly prop fallback while the atom initializes.

The unified GitHub connect entrypoint appends ?github_connected=true to the post-auth URL, which components/home-page-content.tsx reads on mount via useSearchParams, surfaces as a success toast, then strips from the URL with window.history.replaceState so a page refresh does not re-trigger the toast; this is the only signal the connect flow has to confirm to the user that the link succeeded.

getEnabledAuthProviders in lib/auth/providers.ts reads NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_PROVIDERS (a comma-separated list defaulting to 'github') and exposes { github, vercel } booleans that both sign-in dialogs and the connect menu use to decide which buttons render; routes exist and respond regardless of which providers are enabled — there is no per-route allow-list, only a UI-level filter.

components/repo-selector.tsx is a secondary consumer that POSTs to /api/auth/github/disconnect whenever /api/github/user or /api/github/orgs returns 401 or 403, providing a self-healing branch that drops a stale GitHub link without waiting for user interaction; this is the only call site outside the auth UI that triggers disconnect.
